wg-estacionamento.title: WG Estacionamento
wg-estacionamento.label: Custom system · in production
wg-estacionamento.pitch: A management system for a parking lot that opened from scratch and has run on it since day one.
wg-estacionamento.role: API and business rules, in partnership

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: The client was opening a new parking lot with no system at all. They needed to track the lot, charge hourly and monthly customers and close the till from opening day.

sections.heading: What I built
items: Vehicle check-in and check-out by licence plate, with the customer linked by their tax ID.
Hourly charging with a grace period, paid by PIX, card or cash.
Monthly and overnight plans with a fixed due date, pro-rated sign-up and time-limited discounts.
Daily till and a monthly report by payment method.
Admin and operator roles, recording who received each payment.
Manual entries with a past date, to fix forgotten check-ins.

sections.heading: My role
sections.body: Built in partnership with my business partner. I built the API: billing rules, memberships, till, reports and authentication. He built the frontend.

sections.heading: Technical decisions
sections.body: Amounts are always stored in cents and payments run inside database transactions. The API is organised by domain, with Zod validation and Swagger docs. The database evolved through 41 migrations as the client's real needs came up. The system was built ready for more than one location, so the client can open new sites without rework.

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In daily use since opening day in August 2025. By October 2026 it had recorded 8,858 vehicle entries, about 620 a month, and more than 1,600 registered customers across monthly and overnight plans.

zeca.title: Zeca · Innoa Seguros
zeca.label: Current job · lead developer
zeca.pitch: Innoa's health and life benefits management platform, used by the broker's own team and by the HR departments of client companies.

sections.heading: My role
sections.body: I am Innoa's lead developer. Technical decisions, architecture, new ideas and complex problems go through me. I maintain and evolve v1, which is still in production, and lead the build of v2 of the broker area, with a new frontend and API.

sections.heading: What v2 covers
sections.body: Contracts and policyholders, beneficiaries and enrolment changes, support tickets and a deals board to follow each opportunity.

sections.heading: Technical decisions
sections.body: Code organised by context, keeping the broker area and the HR area apart. Two layers of tests: unit and component tests, plus end-to-end tests against a mocked API, so screens can be tested without the backend. CI runs lint, type checks and tests, and commits follow a convention. The v2 backend and frontend move together, one complete feature at a time.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: Cartão Vet is a discount club for pet owners, with monthly and yearly plans that renew automatically. Billing ran on PagSeguro, which no longer served the project well, and support did not respond.

sections.heading: What I did

conserte-car.title: Conserte Car
conserte-car.label: SaaS product
conserte-car.pitch: A management SaaS for car repair shops, born from one client's request and designed from the start to serve many shops.

sections.heading: Context
sections.body: The shop worked with paper, spreadsheets and scattered information, and paid a lot for a system that did not fit its routine.

sections.heading: What I built
items: Work orders with status, priority, the shop's own numbering and a printout with logo and warranty terms.
Customers and vehicles, where a vehicle can have more than one owner.
Parts inventory with minimum and maximum levels, cost and sale price, and movement history linked to work orders.
Service catalogue, mechanics and a dashboard with indicators and low-stock alerts.
Team invitations by email and role-based permissions.

sections.heading: SaaS model
sections.body: Each shop's data is isolated. Sign-up starts a free trial, the subscription renews by PIX with limits per plan, and an expired account becomes read-only instead of losing its data.

sections.heading: Technical decisions
sections.body: Unit and end-to-end tests against a real PostgreSQL. Deployment only happens after lint, type checks and tests pass, with migrations applied first. On the frontend, every API response is validated with Zod.

sections.heading: Validation
sections.body: The first customer used the system and paid the subscription for three months, which validated the whole recurring billing flow.

voltlab.title: VoltLab
voltlab.label: Own product · MVP
voltlab.pitch: A visual editor for home electrical installations that checks the design against the Brazilian NBR 5410 standard.

sections.heading: Who it is for
sections.body: Home owners with everyday doubts, such as the shower that trips the breaker or the cable that gets hot, and electricians who want to see the calculations.

sections.heading: What it does today
items: Draw the installation on a canvas: service entrance, panel, breakers, RCDs, loads and cables.
Check current, cable ampacity, voltage drop, cable and breaker coordination, RCD use and dedicated circuits in real time.
Cite the clause of the standard for each finding and show the calculation.
Mark a result as inconclusive when data is missing, instead of guessing a value.

sections.heading: Technical decisions
sections.body: The calculation engine is plain TypeScript, separate from the interface and covered by tests. It runs in the browser and on the server and follows a technical specification written before the code.

sections.heading: Current stage
sections.body: MVP is live. Results are shown as a preview and do not replace a design by a licensed professional.
